To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an online multi-object tracking system that does not use object-specific prior knowledge to detect and track objects, and we show that by transferring the object-specific knowledge to the classification stage of a video object recognition system, we can improve object classification accuracy.

(1) by transferring the use prior knowledge from detection to classification we can design a general-purpose object recognition system that is competitive with the best systems in the literature, (2) we can design an online tracking system that can track multiple objects without the need for object-specific prior knowledge or user-based track initialisation,
we propose a biologically inspired approach for online multi-object recognition in video that does not require prior knowledge about the objects in the scene.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of online multi-object tracking and recognition in an image sequence and the proposed solution is a biologically inspired approach that does not rely on object-specific prior information in the detection and tracking stage.

the problem of online object recognition in an image sequence, and the proposed solution addresses this problem with a system that is able to track and classify objects in the scene with minimal use of object-specific information.
the design and implementation of a general purpose object recognition algorithm, which is robust to a variety of object shapes and motions.

our proposed approach is able to achieve a high degree of accuracy and robustness in the detection and tracking of objects without relying on any prior knowledge about the objects.

the proposed system is a general purpose object recognition solution that can be applied to a wide variety of object types and is able to adaptively learn the shape and motion information of the tracked objects, which is not possible with other state-of-the-art systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our approach is the first to show how to use a generic object tracker and classifier to achieve state-of-the-art performance on the Neovision benchmark, without the need for any object-specific prior knowledge.
we are able to track multiple objects in a sequence and classify them with a single system.

we have demonstrated the ability of a biologically inspired system to learn object-specific information from the image stream and to use it for object recognition, without requiring any prior object-specific knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by using the tracking stage to limit the prior knowledge used for classification, we can design robust, general purpose systems that can be applied to new object types and new domains.

by limiting the use of prior information in the detection and tracking stage to the bare minimum, and instead using it to inform a classification algorithm that is capable of learning object-specific prior information, we can design an online multi-object recognition system that is robust, general purpose and scalable.

object tracking and recognition can be performed in a unified framework, and that by using the same prior knowledge for both tasks, we can achieve better results than when the two are treated separately.
